sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo gaṇāḥ śatrubhayaṃkarāḥ anujagmur mahātmānaṃ tridaśendrasya saṃmate
english: These and many other hosts, terror to their foes, followed the great-souled one, with the consent of Indra, lord of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktyastram adadad bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ guhāya rājaśārdūla vināśāya suradviṣām
english: Then the blessed Pākaśāsana bestowed the spear-weapon upon Guha, O tiger among kings, for the destruction of the enemies of the gods.

sanskrit: mahāsvanāṃ mahāghaṇṭāṃ dyotamānāṃ sitaprabhām taruṇādityavarṇāṃ ca patākāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: And a banner, loud-resounding, hung with a great bell, blazing, of white radiance and the hue of the young sun, O bull of the Bhāratas—

sanskrit: dadau paśupatis tasmai sarvabhūtamahācamūm ugrāṃ nānāpraharaṇāṃ tapovīryabalānvitām
english: Paśupati gave him that, and a mighty army of all the spirits, fierce, bearing weapons of every kind, endowed with the power of austerity, valor, and strength.

sanskrit: viṣṇur dadau vaijayantīṃ mālāṃ balavivardhinīm umā dadau cārajasī vāsasī sūryasaprabhe
english: Viṣṇu gave the Vaijayantī garland that swells one's strength; Umā gave two spotless garments, gleaming bright as the sun.

sanskrit: gaṅgā kamaṇḍaluṃ divyam amṛtodbhavam uttamam dadau prītyā kumārāya daṇḍaṃ caiva bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Gaṅgā with love gave the prince a divine, supreme water-pot born of the nectar, and Bṛhaspati gave a staff.

sanskrit: garuḍo dayitaṃ putraṃ mayūraṃ citrabarhiṇam aruṇas tāmracūḍaṃ ca pradadau caraṇāyudham
english: Garuḍa gave his beloved son the peacock with its dappled plumage, and Aruṇa gave the red-crested cock, that creature whose weapons are its feet.

sanskrit: pāśaṃ tu varuṇo rājā balavīryasamanvitam kṛṣṇājinaṃ tathā brahmā brahmaṇyāya dadau prabhuḥ samareṣu jayaṃ caiva pradadau lokabhāvanaḥ
english: King Varuṇa gave a noose endowed with strength and valor; and Brahmā the Lord, maker of the worlds, gave a black antelope skin to the devout one, and bestowed victory in battles as well.

sanskrit: senāpatyam anuprāpya skando devagaṇasya ha śuśubhe jvalito 'rciṣmān dvitīya iva pāvakaḥ tataḥ pāriṣadaiś caiva mātṛbhiś ca samanvitaḥ
english: Having attained command over the host of the gods, Skanda shone forth, blazing and flaming like a second fire, surrounded then by his attendants and by the Mothers.

sanskrit: sā senā nairṛtī bhīmā saghaṇṭocchritaketanā sabherīśaṅkhamurajā sāyudhā sapatākinī śāradī dyaur ivābhāti jyotirbhir upaśobhitā
english: That dreadful army of spirits, with bells and uplifted banners, with kettledrums, conches, and tabors, with weapons and standards, shone like the autumn sky adorned with its stars.

sanskrit: tato devanikāyās te bhūtasenāgaṇās tathā vādayām āsur avyagrā bherīśaṅkhāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: Then those companies of the gods and the throngs of the spirit-army, unhurried, sounded their drums and abundant conches,

sanskrit: paṭahāñ jharjharāṃś caiva kṛkacān goviṣāṇikān āḍambarān gomukhāṃś ca ḍiṇḍimāṃś ca mahāsvanān
english: war-drums and rattles, saws and ox-horns, kettledrums and cow-faced trumpets, and tabors of mighty sound.

sanskrit: tuṣṭuvus te kumāraṃ ca sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ jaguś ca devagandharvā nanṛtuś cāpsarogaṇāḥ
english: All the gods with Vāsava praised the prince, the celestial gandharvas sang, and the troops of apsarases danced.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahāsenas tridaśebhyo varaṃ dadau ripūn hantāsmi samare ye vo vadhacikīrṣavaḥ
english: Then the great-armied one, well pleased, granted a boon to the thirty gods: "I shall slay in battle those foes who seek your destruction."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya varaṃ devās tasmād vibudhasattamāt prītātmāno mahātmāno menire nihatān ripūn
english: Receiving the boon from that best of the wise, the great-souled gods, glad at heart, counted their foes as already slain.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ bhūtasaṃghānāṃ harṣān nādaḥ samutthitaḥ apūrayata lokāṃs trīn vare datte mahātmanā
english: When the boon was granted by the great-souled one, a roar of joy arose from all the assembled spirits and filled the three worlds.

sanskrit: sa niryayau mahāseno mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ vadhāya yudhi daityānāṃ rakṣārthaṃ ca divaukasām
english: Then the great-armied one set forth, encircled by his vast army, to slay the daityas in battle and to protect the dwellers of heaven.

sanskrit: vyavasāyo jayo dharmaḥ siddhir lakṣmīr dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ mahāsenasya sainyānām agre jagmur narādhipa
english: Resolve, Victory, Righteousness, Success, Fortune, Constancy, and Memory marched before the armies of the great-armied one, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sa tayā bhīmayā devaḥ śūlamudgarahastayā gadāmusalanārācaśaktitomarahastayā dṛptasiṃhaninādinyā vinadya prayayau guhaḥ
english: With that terrible host—weapons of pike and mace, of club and pestle, of iron shaft, spear, and lance in its hands—roaring like a proud lion, the god Guha bellowed and went forth.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvadaiteyā rākṣasā dānavās tathā vyadravanta diśaḥ sarvā bhayodvignāḥ samantataḥ abhyadravanta devās tān vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ
english: Seeing him, all the daiteyas, rākṣasas, and dānavas fled in every direction, agitated with fear on every side; and the gods, weapons of every kind in hand, rushed upon them.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca sa tataḥ kruddhaḥ skandas tejobalānvitaḥ śaktyastraṃ bhagavān bhīmaṃ punaḥ punar avāsṛjat ādadhac cātmanas tejo haviṣeddha ivānalaḥ
english: And the blessed Skanda, beholding this, was enraged; endowed with splendor and strength, he hurled the dreadful spear-weapon again and again, kindling his own brilliance like a fire fed with oblation.

sanskrit: abhyasyamāne śaktyastre skandenāmitatejasā ulkājvālā mahārāja papāta vasudhātale
english: As the spear-weapon was being hurled by Skanda of measureless brilliance, blazing meteors fell, O great king, upon the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: saṃhrādayantaś ca tathā nirghātāś cāpatan kṣitau yathāntakālasamaye sughorāḥ syus tathā nṛpa
english: And crashing thunderbolts fell upon the ground, as fearsome as those at the hour of the world's end, O king.

sanskrit: kṣiptā hy ekā tathā śaktiḥ sughorānalasūnunā tataḥ koṭyo viniṣpetuḥ śaktīnāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: A single spear was hurled by the dread son of fire, and from it sprang forth tens of millions of spears, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa śaktyastreṇa saṃgrāme jaghāna bhagavān prabhuḥ daityendraṃ tārakaṃ nāma mahābalaparākramam vṛtaṃ daityāyutair vīrair balibhir daśabhir nṛpa
english: With that spear-weapon the blessed Lord slew in battle the daitya-king named Tāraka, of mighty strength and prowess, surrounded by a hundred thousand valiant daityas and by ten mighty warriors, O king.

sanskrit: mahiṣaṃ cāṣṭabhiḥ padmair vṛtaṃ saṃkhye nijaghnivān tripādaṃ cāyutaśatair jaghāna daśabhir vṛtam
english: He smote down Mahiṣa, encircled in battle by eight hundred billion, and slew Tripāda, surrounded by ten times a million times a hundred thousand.

sanskrit: hradodaraṃ nikharvaiś ca vṛtaṃ daśabhir īśvaraḥ jaghānānucaraiḥ sārdhaṃ vividhāyudhapāṇibhiḥ
english: And the Lord slew Hradodara, encircled by ten hundred billion, together with his followers bearing weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: tatrākurvanta vipulaṃ nādaṃ vadhyatsu śatruṣu kumārānucarā rājan pūrayanto diśo daśa
english: There, as the foes were being slain, the prince's followers raised a mighty roar, O king, filling the ten directions.

sanskrit: śaktyastrasya tu rājendra tato 'rcirbhiḥ samantataḥ dagdhāḥ sahasraśo daityā nādaiḥ skandasya cāpare
english: By the flames of the spear-weapon on every side, O lord of kings, the daityas were burned by the thousand, and others by the war-cries of Skanda.

sanskrit: patākayāvadhūtāś ca hatāḥ ke cit suradviṣaḥ ke cid ghaṇṭāravatrastā nipetur vasudhātale ke cit praharaṇaiś chinnā vinipetur gatāsavaḥ
english: Some enemies of the gods, struck down by the lashing of the banner, were slain; some, terrified by the clang of the bell, fell upon the earth; and some, cleft by weapons, dropped down lifeless.

sanskrit: evaṃ suradviṣo 'nekān balavān ātatāyinaḥ jaghāna samare vīraḥ kārttikeyo mahābalaḥ
english: Thus the heroic Kārttikeya, mighty and strong, slew in battle many a powerful and aggressive foe of the gods.

sanskrit: bāṇo nāmātha daiteyo baleḥ putro mahābalaḥ krauñcaṃ parvatam āsādya devasaṃghān abādhata
english: Now a daiteya named Bāṇa, the son of Bali, of mighty strength, took to Mount Krauñca and harassed the hosts of the gods.

sanskrit: tam abhyayān mahāsenaḥ suraśatrum udāradhīḥ sa kārttikeyasya bhayāt krauñcaṃ śaraṇam eyivān
english: The great-armied one, lofty of mind, advanced upon that enemy of the gods; and out of fear of Kārttikeya he took refuge in Krauñca.

sanskrit: tataḥ krauñcaṃ mahāmanyuḥ krauñcanādanināditam śaktyā bibheda bhagavān kārttikeyo 'gnidattayā
english: Then the blessed Kārttikeya, full of great wrath, clove Krauñca—resounding with the cry of the krauñca-bird—with the spear given by Agni.

sanskrit: saśālaskandhasaralaṃ trastavānaravāraṇam pulinatrastavihagaṃ viniṣpatitapannagam
english: With its sāl trunks and pines, with elephants of the forest in panic, with birds startled from its riverbanks and serpents tumbling forth,

sanskrit: golāṅgūlarkṣasaṃghaiś ca dravadbhir anunāditam kuraṅgagatinirghoṣam udbhrāntasṛmarācitam
english: echoing with troops of fleeing langurs and bears, loud with the rush of running deer, thronged with bewildered wild oxen,

sanskrit: viniṣpatadbhiḥ śarabhaiḥ siṃhaiś ca sahasā drutaiḥ śocyām api daśāṃ prāpto rarājaiva sa parvataḥ
english: with śarabhas and lions suddenly bursting forth and fleeing—though fallen into a pitiable state, that mountain still shone in splendor.

sanskrit: vidyādharāḥ samutpetus tasya śṛṅganivāsinaḥ kiṃnarāś ca samudvignāḥ śaktipātaravoddhatāḥ
english: The vidyādharas who dwelt upon its peaks flew up, and the kiṃnaras too, terrified and startled by the roar of the falling spear.

sanskrit: tato daityā viniṣpetuḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ pradīptāt parvataśreṣṭhād vicitrābharaṇasrajaḥ
english: Then the daityas, in their hundreds and thousands, decked in gleaming ornaments and garlands, rushed forth from that blazing best of mountains.

sanskrit: tān nijaghnur atikramya kumārānucarā mṛdhe bibheda śaktyā krauñcaṃ ca pāvakiḥ paravīrahā
english: The prince's followers overtook and slew them in the fray, and the son of fire, slayer of hostile heroes, clove Krauñca with his spear.

sanskrit: bahudhā caikadhā caiva kṛtvātmānaṃ mahātmanā śaktiḥ kṣiptā raṇe tasya pāṇim eti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Making itself now manifold, now single, the spear hurled in battle by the great-souled one returned to his hand again and again.

sanskrit: evaṃprabhāvo bhagavān ato bhūyaś ca pāvakiḥ krauñcas tena vinirbhinno daityāś ca śataśo hatāḥ
english: Of such power was the blessed son of fire, and greater still: by him Krauñca was riven asunder and the daityas were slain by the hundred.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān devo nihatya vibudhadviṣaḥ sabhājyamāno vibudhaiḥ paraṃ harṣam avāpa ha
english: Then the blessed god, having slain the enemies of the gods, honored by the gods, attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: tato dundubhayo rājan neduḥ śaṅkhāś ca bhārata mumucur devayoṣāś ca puṣpavarṣam anuttamam
english: Then the kettledrums sounded, O king, and the conches, O Bhārata, and the women of the gods let fall an incomparable rain of flowers.

sanskrit: divyagandham upādāya vavau puṇyaś ca mārutaḥ gandharvās tuṣṭuvuś cainaṃ yajvānaś ca maharṣayaḥ
english: A holy breeze blew, bearing a celestial fragrance, and the gandharvas praised him, as did the sacrificing great seers.

sanskrit: ke cid enaṃ vyavasyanti pitāmahasutaṃ prabhum sanatkumāraṃ sarveṣāṃ brahmayoniṃ tam agrajam
english: Some declare him to be the Lord, the son of the Grandsire, Sanatkumāra, the first-born of all, sprung from Brahman;

sanskrit: ke cin maheśvarasutaṃ ke cit putraṃ vibhāvasoḥ umāyāḥ kṛttikānāṃ ca gaṅgāyāś ca vadanty uta
english: some the son of Maheśvara, some the son of Vibhāvasu; and they speak of him also as the son of Umā, of the Kṛttikās, and of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: ekadhā ca dvidhā caiva caturdhā ca mahābalam yoginām īśvaraṃ devaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: The mighty one, lord of yogins, that god—one and twofold and fourfold, and in his hundreds and thousands of forms.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ rājan kārttikeyābhiṣecanam śṛṇu caiva sarasvatyās tīrthavaṃśasya puṇyatām
english: Thus has the consecration of Kārttikeya been told to you, O king; now hear the holiness of the lineage of fords of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: babhūva tīrthapravaraṃ hateṣu suraśatruṣu kumāreṇa mahārāja triviṣṭapam ivāparam
english: When the enemies of the gods had been slain by the prince, there arose a most excellent ford, O great king, like a second heaven.

sanskrit: aiśvaryāṇi ca tatrastho dadāv īśaḥ pṛthak pṛthak tadā nairṛtamukhyebhyas trailokye pāvakātmajaḥ
english: And dwelling there, the Lord, the son of fire, then bestowed dominions, each in turn, upon the chief spirits throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavāṃs tasmiṃs tīrthe daityakulāntakaḥ abhiṣikto mahārāja devasenāpatiḥ suraiḥ
english: Thus was the blessed one, the ender of the daitya race, consecrated at that ford by the gods as commander of the host of heaven, O great king.

sanskrit: aujasaṃ nāma tat tīrthaṃ yatra pūrvam apāṃ patiḥ abhiṣiktaḥ suragaṇair varuṇo bharatarṣabha
english: That ford is named Aujasa, where of old the lord of waters, Varuṇa, was consecrated by the hosts of the gods, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthavare snātvā skandaṃ cābhyarcya lāṅgalī brāhmaṇebhyo dadau rukmaṃ vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: Having bathed at that most excellent ford and worshipped Skanda, the Plough-bearer gave gold, garments, and ornaments to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: uṣitvā rajanīṃ tatra mādhavaḥ paravīrahā pūjya tīrthavaraṃ tac ca spṛṣṭvā toyaṃ ca lāṅgalī hṛṣṭaḥ prītamanāś caiva hy abhavan mādhavottamaḥ
english: Having passed the night there, Mādhava, slayer of hostile heroes, the Plough-bearer, worshipped that excellent ford and touched its waters; and that best of the Mādhavas became glad and joyful at heart.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi yathābhiṣikto bhagavān skando devaiḥ samāgataiḥ
english: All this has been told to you, that which you asked of me—how the blessed Skanda was consecrated by the assembled gods.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca atyadbhutam idaṃ brahmañ śrutavān asmi tattvataḥ abhiṣekaṃ kumārasya vistareṇa yathāvidhi
english: Janamejaya said: Most wondrous is this, O brāhmaṇa; I have heard truly and in full detail the consecration of the prince, just as it was ordained.

sanskrit: yac chrutvā pūtam ātmānaṃ vijānāmi tapodhana prahṛṣṭāni ca romāṇi prasannaṃ ca mano mama
english: Hearing it, I know my very self to be purified, O treasury of austerity; the hairs of my body stand thrilled, and my mind is serene.

sanskrit: abhiṣekaṃ kumārasya daityānāṃ ca vadhaṃ tathā śrutvā me paramā prītir bhūyaś ca kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: At hearing the consecration of the prince and the slaying of the daityas, my joy is supreme—and my curiosity is greater still.

sanskrit: apāṃ patiḥ kathaṃ hy asminn abhiṣiktaḥ surāsuraiḥ tan me brūhi mahāprājña kuśalo hy asi sattama
english: How was the lord of waters consecrated here by gods and asuras? Tell me that, O greatly wise one, for you are skilled, O best of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇu rājann idaṃ citraṃ pūrvakalpe yathātatham ādau kṛtayuge tasmin vartamāne yathāvidhi varuṇaṃ devatāḥ sarvāḥ sametyedam athābruvan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hear, O king, this marvel just as it was in a former age. Of old, while that first age, the Kṛtayuga, ran its course in due order, all the deities came together and spoke thus to Varuṇa:

sanskrit: yathāsmān surarāṭ śakro bhayebhyaḥ pāti sarvadā tathā tvam api sarvāsāṃ saritāṃ vai patir bhava
english: "As Śakra, king of the gods, ever guards us from dangers, so do you too become the lord of all the rivers.

sanskrit: vāsaś ca te sadā deva sāgare makarālaye samudro 'yaṃ tava vaśe bhaviṣyati nadīpatiḥ
english: And your dwelling shall ever be, O god, in the ocean, abode of the sea-monsters; this sea, lord of streams, shall be under your sway.

sanskrit: somena sārdhaṃ ca tava hānivṛddhī bhaviṣyataḥ evam astv iti tān devān varuṇo vākyam abravīt
english: And with Soma your waning and waxing shall come to pass." "So be it," said Varuṇa in answer to those gods.

sanskrit: samāgamya tataḥ sarve varuṇaṃ sāgarālayam apāṃ patiṃ pracakrur hi vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Then all of them, coming together, made Varuṇa, dweller in the ocean, the lord of waters, by rites prescribed in the ordinance.

sanskrit: abhiṣicya tato devā varuṇaṃ yādasāṃ patim jagmuḥ svāny eva sthānāni pūjayitvā jaleśvaram
english: Having consecrated Varuṇa as lord of the water-creatures and honored the lord of waters, the gods then went each to his own abode.

sanskrit: abhiṣiktas tato devair varuṇo 'pi mahāyaśāḥ saritaḥ sāgarāṃś caiva nadāṃś caiva sarāṃsi ca pālayām āsa vidhinā yathā devāñ śatakratuḥ
english: Consecrated by the gods, the greatly glorious Varuṇa governed the rivers and seas, the streams and the lakes, by rule, even as the Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices governs the gods.

sanskrit: tatas tatrāpy upaspṛśya dattvā ca vividhaṃ vasu agnitīrthaṃ mahāprājñaḥ sa jagāma pralambahā naṣṭo na dṛśyate yatra śamīgarbhe hutāśanaḥ
english: Then, having touched the water there too and given wealth of many kinds, the greatly wise slayer of Pralamba went to the Agni-tīrtha, where the oblation-eater, hidden in the heart of the śamī tree, had vanished and could not be seen.

sanskrit: lokālokavināśe ca prādurbhūte tadānagha upatasthur mahātmānaṃ sarvalokapitāmaham
english: And when the destruction of light and darkness throughout the worlds had come to pass, O sinless one, the gods drew near the great-souled Grandsire of all the worlds.

sanskrit: agniḥ pranaṣṭo bhagavān kāraṇaṃ ca na vidmahe sarvalokakṣayo mā bhūt saṃpādayatu no 'nalam
english: "The blessed fire has vanished, and we do not know the cause; let there be no destruction of all the worlds—restore the fire to us."

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kimarthaṃ bhagavān agniḥ pranaṣṭo lokabhāvanaḥ vijñātaś ca kathaṃ devais tan mamācakṣva tattvataḥ
english: Janamejaya said: Why did the blessed fire, sustainer of the worlds, vanish, and how was it found out by the gods? Tell me that truly.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhṛgoḥ śāpād bhṛśaṃ bhīto jātavedāḥ pratāpavān śamīgarbham athāsādya nanāśa bhagavāṃs tataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Sorely afraid by reason of the curse of Bhṛgu, the mighty Jātavedas, entering the heart of the śamī tree, the blessed one thereupon vanished.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭe tu tadā vahnau devāḥ sarve savāsavāḥ anveṣanta tadā naṣṭaṃ jvalanaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: When the fire had thus vanished, all the gods with Vāsava, sorely grieved, then searched for the lost flame.

sanskrit: tato 'gnitīrtham āsādya śamīgarbhastham eva hi dadṛśur jvalanaṃ tatra vasamānaṃ yathāvidhi
english: Then, reaching the Agni-tīrtha, they beheld the flame there dwelling, after its own manner, within the heart of the śamī tree.

sanskrit: devāḥ sarve naravyāghra bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ jvalanaṃ taṃ samāsādya prītābhūvan savāsavāḥ punar yathāgataṃ jagmuḥ sarvabhakṣaś ca so 'bhavat
english: All the gods, O tiger among men, with Bṛhaspati at their head and with Vāsava, drew near that flame and were gladdened; they returned each as they had come, and that fire became the devourer of all.

sanskrit: bhṛgoḥ śāpān mahīpāla yad uktaṃ brahmavādinā tatrāpy āplutya matimān brahmayoniṃ jagāma ha
english: By the curse of Bhṛgu, O guardian of the earth, that which was spoken by the knower of Brahman came to pass; and having bathed there too, the wise one went to the source of Brahman.

sanskrit: sasarja bhagavān yatra sarvalokapitāmahaḥ tatrāplutya tato brahmā saha devaiḥ prabhuḥ purā sasarja cānnāni tathā devatānāṃ yathāvidhi
english: There, where the blessed Grandsire of all the worlds had brought forth creation, having bathed, the Lord Brahmā with the gods of old created the foods of the deities, each in due order.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā ca dattvā ca vasūni vividhāni ca kauberaṃ prayayau tīrthaṃ tatra taptvā mahat tapaḥ dhanādhipatyaṃ saṃprāpto rājann ailabilaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Having bathed there and bestowed wealth of many kinds, he went on to the tīrtha of Kubera, where, having performed great austerity, the Lord, son of Ilabilā, attained the sovereignty over riches, O king.

sanskrit: tatrastham eva taṃ rājan dhanāni nidhayas tathā upatasthur naraśreṣṭha tat tīrthaṃ lāṅgalī tataḥ gatvā snātvā ca vidhivad brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ dadau
english: Even as he abode there, O king, riches and treasures waited upon him, O best of men; and the Plough-bearer, having gone to that tīrtha and bathed according to rule, gave wealth to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: dadṛśe tatra tat sthānaṃ kaubere kānanottame purā yatra tapas taptaṃ vipulaṃ sumahātmanā
english: There in Kubera's domain, in that loveliest of forests, he beheld that place where of old great austerity had been performed by the exalted one.
